name: Work Permit (Employer-Specific LMIA & LMIA-Exempt IMP)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a job offer and a positive Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) — the employer must advertise the role and prove no Canadian/PR was available, and pay a $1,000/position LMIA fee to ESDC.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer from an employer willing to complete the LMIA process.

requirements.blocker_text: This covers CUSMA/USMCA professionals, traders and investors, general intra-company transferees (1 year foreign employment in the past 3 years with a qualifying corporate relationship), CETA/CPTPP categories, Francophone Mobility, International Experience Canada, and other LMIA-exempt categories — still requires an Offer of Employment filed via the Employer Portal plus a $230 compliance fee.

evidence_required.document: Positive LMIA (LMIA-based group) or documented LMIA exemption category evidence (IMP group)

outcome.duration_length: up to the duration of the LMIA or exemption category, typically 1-3 years

sources.title: Temporary Foreign Worker Program - Employment and Social Development Canada

notes: GENUINE GOVERNMENT PREFERENCE confirmed: 2026 targets reportedly favor LMIA-exempt IMP routes over LMIA-based TFWP by a wide margin (~170,000 vs ~60,000 admissions per tier-3 reporting) — the government is explicitly steering employers toward the lighter-touch IMP wherever a qualifying exemption applies. CUSMA professionals (US/Mexican nationals) can often get same-day permits at a land port of entry — a genuinely fast-track mechanic not seen elsewhere in this dataset for a work-sponsored route. leads_to_pr is FALSE at the route level since neither LMIA-based nor most IMP work permits grant PR directly — the real path is accumulating Canadian work experience then applying via ca_express_entry_cec or ca_pnp, the same temporary-then-PR staging common across most European countries in this dataset, in contrast to Express Entry's own direct-to-PR design.
